US10870621B2_latanoprostene_bunod.note: Six pages, 411 kB, about 27 depictions and NOT ONE non-structure figure - the front page says '8 Claims, No Drawings' and here that is nearly literal, yet every page after the first is chemistry. Rough page tally from a 65-dpi sheet: p2 formula (1) plus prior-art Reaction Scheme 1 (~5); p3 Reaction Scheme 2, the invention's route (~8); p4 formulae (2), (3), (5) (~5); p5 the Example structures (~4); p6 the claim structures (~5). THE POINT OF THIS GROUP IS STEREOCHEMISTRY: latanoprostene bunod carries FIVE tetrahedral stereocentres (1R,2R,3R,5S on the cyclopentane and R on the pentyl side chain) plus a cis (Z) alkene, all drawn as wedges with the full stereo-descriptor set also printed in the name. Every intermediate in the route carries the same five.

US11597692B2_tapinarof.drawing_style: USPTO scan (libtiff/tiff2pdf), NO text layer. Very dense inline ChemDraw art; trans-stilbene and diene geometries drawn explicitly, and formula (IIa) carries a SQUIGGLY (wavy) bond on its chlorine
US11597692B2_tapinarof.note: PAGE EXTRACT. The corpus file is not the whole publication: pages 1-12,30,36-40 of the 40-page original were kept with `mutool merge -o US11597692B2_tapinarof.pdf <original>.pdf 1-12,30,36-40`, which keeps the front page, every structure-bearing page, at least one page of each non-structure figure class the document contains, and the claims. EVERY PAGE NUMBER IN THIS GROUP - in molecules[].page, in unscoreable[].page and in the prose of this note - REFERS TO THE ORIGINAL PUBLISHED DOCUMENT, not to the extract. `structures_drawn` also counts the original. One of the two most structure-dense documents in the round: roughly 110 depictions across pp5-40 with only TWO non-structure sheets (pp3-4, both PXRD). Estimate from a 45-dpi contact sheet. The route runs cinnamaldehyde -> a dienone -> a malonate Michael adduct -> the malonic acid -> a chlorinated cyclohexane-1,3-dione -> aromatisation to tapinarof, and every stage is drawn many times over across the Summary, the numbered embodiments and the claims. Formula (IIa) is the one to notice: its C2 bears BOTH an isopropyl and a chlorine, and the chlorine is drawn on a WAVY BOND - an explicitly undefined stereocentre, a third stereo convention beyond bold/hashed wedges and printed CIP letters.

The corpus file is not the whole publication: pages 1-3,7,10,20-22,26,30-33,36 of the 36-page original were kept with `mutool merge -o US20230002439A1_vamorolone.pdf <original>.pdf 1-3,7,10,20-22,26,30-33,36`, which keeps the front page, every structure-bearing page, at least one page of each non-structure figure class the document contains, and the claims. EVERY PAGE NUMBER IN THIS GROUP - in molecules[].page, in unscoreable[].page and in the prose of this note - REFERS TO THE ORIGINAL PUBLISHED DOCUMENT, not to the extract. `structures_drawn` also counts the original. THE ROUND'S STEROID GROUP, and the one where the stereochemical near-miss is most dangerous - vamorolone has five tetrahedral stereocentres and its drawing distinguishes them only by wedge type plus two lettered ring-junction hydrogens. Twenty numbered drawing sheets on pp2-21 (PXRD patterns stacked as upper/lower pairs against Form I, TGA profiles, DSC profiles) and, on p21, a greyscale RASTER HEATMAP of the polymorph screen - a solid-fill grid image, a figure class nothing else in the round has. unscoreable.note: A CAPTION/STRUCTURE MISMATCH, and the most interesting thing in the group. The seventh box of FIG. 1 is drawn as an ESTER-PROTECTED ether of the 3-iodo-4-hydroxybiphenyl-4'-carbonitrile - an acetate on an oxyalkyl chain hanging off the phenol oxygen - but its printed caption repeats '4-((4-bromo-2-(tert-butyl)phenyl) amino)-4-oxobutanoic acid', which is the caption of box 2 one row above and describes a completely different molecule with a bromine and a tert-butyl. The name and the drawing are two identity signals and they disagree, so this box stays unresolved. (It is also the only box whose methylene count could not be read with certainty at 150 dpi.) A pipeline that trusts a nearby caption over the drawing will emit the wrong molecule here and be scored wrong for the right reason.

US11370739B2_sacubitril.note: SINGLE-PAGE EXTRACT of the 39-page grant 'SACUBITRIL INTERMEDIATE AND PREPARATION METHOD THEREOF'. p2 is the first page of the description and carries all three depictions: sacubitril itself, drawn with one hashed and one bold wedge, and two Boc-protected biphenyl intermediates drawn with WAVY bonds. THE POINT OF THE PAGE IS THAT ONE DOCUMENT USES THREE DIFFERENT STEREO NOTATIONS WITHIN 8 CM: a hashed wedge, a bold wedge, and a wavy bond meaning 'undefined'. The wavy bond is the interesting one - it is a positive assertion that the centre is NOT defined, so the correct reference is the stereo-unspecified PubChem record, and a tool that reads the squiggle as a plain bond gets the same answer while a tool that reads it as a wedge gets a different, real, wrong record. Both intermediates resolve to stereo-unspecified CIDs.

THE POINT OF THIS DOCUMENT IS STEREOCHEMISTRY. Every example title prints an explicit CIP letter, every stereocentre carries a drawn wedge or hash, and FOUR of the compounds have a real PubChem record for BOTH enantiomers with the same skeleton InChIKey block - (S)- and (R)-1-azido-5-bromoindane are CID 86638803 and CID 59179602, the two CBS catalysts are CID 2734713 and CID 9838490. Reading the drawing at 400 dpi: the ring-fusion CH carries a BOLD WEDGE to H, and working the CIP priorities N > C(O,C,C) > CH2 > H with the lowest priority toward the viewer gives 3aS, i.e. PubChem CID 2734713, InChIKey VMKAFJQFKBASMU-KRWDZBQOSA-N. Taking the printed 'R' instead gives CID 9838490, '(R)-2-Methyl-CBS-oxazaborolidine', VMKAFJQFKBASMU-QGZVFWFLSA-N - a different real record, same skeleton block. The two views do not agree, so no reference is assigned. This is the round's cleanest instance of the round-6 lesson: a wrong stereo descriptor resolves cleanly to the wrong molecule.

Working the CIP priorities at C6 (the ring N on the NMe2 side outranks the ring N on the NH2 side, because at the next shell NMe2 gives (C,C) against NH2's (H,H)) with H pointing away gives R, agreeing with the printed (6R)

PubChem stores the amino tautomer, which is what the drawing shows. A reader who follows the name rather than the picture produces a different InChI.

WO2024167899A1_milvexian.drawing_style: WIPO A1 scan of a Bristol-Myers Squibb PCT filed in English (PCT/US2024/014585); bitonal full-page raster, no text layer. A single fine-stroke MACROCYCLE drawn with the ring closing through three heteroaromatic systems, two bold wedges, and a difluoromethyl written as a bare CHF2 skeleton (two F labels on one carbon)
WO2024167899A1_milvexian.note: SINGLE-PAGE EXTRACT of the 99-page A1 'MILVEXIAN PHARMACEUTICAL COMPOSITIONS'. p3 carries Formula (I), the only structure in the document. THE REASON FOR THE SLOT IS THE MACROCYCLE: milvexian's 12-membered ring is closed through a pyridine C2, a pyrazole C5 and a lactam N-H, so the macrocyclic bond path is not a visually obvious loop - it runs through three fused-looking heteroaryls and back through an alkyl chain. Round 6 had no macrocycle and the corpus's only other one is the CC-BY review PMC11771699; this is the first macrocyclic drug drawn inside a patent here. Nine nitrogens in four distinct environments (triazole, pyrimidinone, pyridine, pyrazole) plus a lactam, two chlorines on two different rings, and a CHF2 on a ring nitrogen.

WO2024201358A1_pemafibrate.drawing_style: WIPO A1 scan of an Ami Lifesciences PCT filed in English (PCT/IB2024/053015); bitonal full-page raster, no text layer. Medium-weight ChemDraw art with condensed HO / O / N labels, the benzoxazole drawn as a fused bicycle with explicit N and O, and both stereocentres drawn as HASHED wedges to an oxygen
WO2024201358A1_pemafibrate.note: TWO-PAGE EXTRACT of the 26-page A1 'A PROCESS FOR THE PREPARATION OF PEMAFIBRATE AND INTERMEDIATES THEREOF'. Kept: p6 (Formulae I, II, III, IV and V) and p7 (Formula VI). All six depictions catalogued, so the group is scoreable for precision as well as recall, and every one of the six carries a chemical name printed somewhere in the same document. THE POINT OF THIS DOCUMENT is a MITSUNOBU INVERSION drawn in full: Formula-V is ethyl (2S)-2-hydroxybutanoate with its OH on a hashed wedge, and Formula-VI and Formula-I are the (2R) products with their ether oxygen on a hashed wedge in the same drawn orientation. The picture therefore shows the same-looking hash on both sides of a step that inverts the centre - the descriptor changes because the OH became an OR, not because the drawing changed - and the (2S) ester of Formula-VI does not exist in PubChem at all (CID 0), so guessing it is a silent miss rather than a wrong-record hit.

molecules.note: TAUTOMER WARNING. PubChem CID 153284400 stores this amidine with the double bond EXOCYCLIC (C=N-CH2R, ring N-H); the drawing puts it INSIDE the ring (N1=C2, exocyclic N-H). InChI's mobile-H treatment maps the two onto one record, so the structure search succeeds, but the two SMILES strings are different and only the one recorded here reproduces the drawing. A second problem: formulas (III) and (III-S) are drawn IDENTICALLY - both with the hash - so no reading of this document can tell the racemate label from the enantiopure one.

unscoreable.note: THE INTERESTING STRATUM. Each of these is fully drawn AND carries a printed ESI-MS m/z, and the hand reading reproduces the printed mass to 0.01 Da every time: 1-B calc [M+H]+ 474.20 vs printed 474.20; 1-D calc 356.14 vs printed 356.13; and 1-C calc 410.13 for the drawn HYDROCHLORIDE (free base 374.15 + HCl 35.98) vs printed 410.13, which confirms the counter-ion as well as the skeleton. They are left unresolved rather than entered on a hand reading alone. A future round with a mass-based acceptance rule could promote them.

molecules.note: THE CAPTION IS A HEDGE. It says 'Similar to DSP-2230', not 'is DSP-2230'. The reference here was pinned by reading the drawing and comparing it with the DSP-2230 record, NOT by trusting the caption. If the intent was to draw a close analogue rather than the compound itself, this row is wrong - which is why it is flagged rather than left silent.

unscoreable.label: the squiggly-fragment compound table
unscoreable.note: THE DEFINING STRATUM OF THIS GROUP, and the largest depiction class in it. The numbered analogue table draws, for each compound, ONLY the variable fragment - a morpholine, an oxazepane, a trifluoroethoxy pyridine - terminated by a SQUIGGLY (wavy) bond marking where it joins the invariant 6-[3-chloro-4-(cyclopropylmethoxy)phenyl]pyridazine-4-carboxamide core. The full IUPAC name and an ES+ m/z sit in adjacent columns, so the MOLECULE is fully specified in text while the DRAWING is a fragment with an open valence. A tool that emits the drawing emits a radical; a tool that emits the named molecule emits something not drawn. Same failure mode as the round-6 auristatin fragments, but here paired with a complete printed name for every entry. Roughly 150 such fragments in the full grant, about 25 on the three pages kept.

unscoreable.name: pritelivir maleate (formula (I), the CLAIMED compound)

molecules.name: taniborbactam
molecules.label: Compound 1, closed cyclic form
molecules.basis: The full chemical name is printed at [0005] and repeated in every claim: '(R)-3-(2-(trans-4-(2-aminoethylamino)cyclohexyl)acetamido)-2-hydroxy-3,4-dihydro-2H-benzo[e][1,2]oxaborinine-8-carboxylic acid'. Read off the p3 clipping at 5x: an aminoethylamino group on a cyclohexane (N on a HASHED wedge, the CH2CH2CO arm on a BOLD wedge - trans-1,4), an acetamido bridge to a stereocentre drawn with a bold wedge to N-H, a B-OH inside a six-membered B-O-aryl ring fused to a benzene that carries a free CO2H
molecules.note: SILENT STEREO NORMALISATION - the most dangerous thing in this group. The document says trans-4-cyclohexyl in words AND draws it trans (hashed + bold). PubChem CID 76902493 does NOT encode the cyclohexane at all: its own InChIKey is PFZUWUXKQPRWAL-PXCJXSSVSA-N (undefined). Submitting the trans-specified SMILES (PFZUWUXKQPRWAL-BJJXKVORSA-N) to PUG-REST /compound/smiles/ returns CID 76902493 anyway, with nothing in the response saying the query carried stereochemistry the record does not. So a FAITHFUL reading of this drawing scores stereo, not exact, against this reference, and a tool that drops the cyclohexane wedges scores exact. That is a property of the reference, not of the prediction.

molecules.name: taniborbactam dihydrochloride
molecules.label: Compound 1-dihydrochloride salt, '(HCl)2'
molecules.basis: [0148] 'Example 1: Preparation of Compound 1-dihydrochloride Salt'; the p21 product drawing carries the free-floating text label '(HCl)2' beside the structure. Both the name route (PubChem name 'taniborbactam dihydrochloride') and a SMILES structure search return CID 137331954, InChIKey CKWIMFZHNCBHIX-PPJOBQAPSA-N
molecules.note: SALT NOTATION TRAP. The claimed compound is the DIHYDROCHLORIDE, but seven of the ten depictions - every one outside Example 1 - draw only the free base with no counterion, and the salt exists solely in the surrounding words. Only p21 draws it, and it writes the counterions as the condensed text '(HCl)2', not as two dot-separated components.

THE POINT OF THIS GROUP is the pair structure. Examples 5 and 6 share the InChIKey block QEKFYNVTISONGC and differ only in the hydroxyl stereocentre; 7 and 8 share RMWYAYFMEWWLSK; 11 and 12 share BGZJNJSMIAKQIL. Independently, 5 and 7 have the SAME molecular formula C21H22FN5O3 and the same atoms and differ only in whether the propyl chain is bonded to tetrazole N-1 or N-2 - a bond that moves one position around a four-nitrogen ring. A tool that gets the tetrazole regiochemistry wrong lands on the other real record, and a tool that ignores the wedge lands on the diastereomer, so each of the four errors is a confident wrong answer rather than a miss.
